questions.prompt: How often does Rustam visit? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I visit twice a week” — haftada ikki marta.

questions.prompt: What does his sister do? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “She takes photos for the shelter website” — surat oladi.

questions.prompt: What does Rustam bring? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I always bring clean towels” — toza sochiqlar.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqada ko‘ngilli xizmatini tanishtiring, so‘ng sherikning ikki savoliga javob bering.
success: Ikki tasdiq va bir inkor odat gapi bor.
Do/does bilan savol-javob egaga mos.
Bir chastota va bitta aniq joy aytiladi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda kitob aravachasi loyihasiga yangi ko‘ngilli uchun xat yozing.
writing.model: Our book cart visits the park every Sunday. We don't sell books. People borrow them and return them the next week. Malika writes readers' names in a notebook. Her brother repairs the covers. I push the cart and put the books on a small table. Do you enjoy stories? Our team needs another reader. Children usually arrive before the adults. We meet by the fountain at ten. The work is simple, and the readers are friendly. One child brings a toy dragon. It is our quietest club member.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Xizmatning vaqti, joyi va uch vazifasi berilgan.
Tasdiq, inkor, savol va chastota ravishi to‘g‘ri.

teacherNote: Oldindan: borrow — vaqtincha olmoq, fountain — favvora, shelter — hayvonlar boshpanasi. 6-kun: readingdan xizmat kartasini mustaqil tuzdiring; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib javoblarni dalil bilan tekshiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga vazifa–odam jadvali; ilg‘orga o‘xshash yangi xizmatni himoya qilish. Natijani ichki mashq sifatida yozing, standart imtihon bali bermang.

objective: Am/is/are + -ing bilan hozirgi harakatni tasdiq va inkorda tasvirlayman.

reading.title: The Mural in Progress
reading.text: Our class is painting a mural in the corridor. I am drawing a river. Two friends are colouring the hills. Our teacher is holding the paint tray. She isn't painting today. Aziz is cleaning a brush. He isn't washing the floor, although his shoes are very wet. A younger class is watching from the door. We aren't making a perfect picture. We are making a picture together, and everyone has a place in it.

questions.prompt: What is the narrator drawing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I am drawing a river” — daryo chizmoqda.

questions.prompt: Who is holding the tray? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Our teacher is holding the paint tray” — ustoz.

questions.prompt: Is Aziz washing the floor? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “He isn't washing the floor” — pol yuvmayapti.

listening.title: At the Bus Stop Now
listening.text:
Nodira: I am waiting at the bus stop. The rain is starting.
Friend: I am coming from the shop. I am carrying an umbrella.
Nodira: Three people are standing under the little roof. A dog is sitting beside them.
Friend: Is the bus coming?
Nodira: No. It isn't coming yet. The driver is talking to a mechanic across the road.
Friend: I am walking quickly. Your umbrella service is arriving on foot!

questions.prompt: Where is Nodira waiting? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I am waiting at the bus stop” — bekatda.

questions.prompt: What is the friend carrying? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I am carrying an umbrella” — soyabon.

questions.prompt: Who is the driver talking to? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Talking to a mechanic” — mexanik bilan.

speaking.prompt: Devoriy rasm jarayonini 60 soniya jonli tasvirlang: to‘rt ish va bajarilmayotgan ikki ishni ayting.
success: Am/is/are egaga mos.
To‘rtta harakat -ing shaklida.
Isn't/aren't bilan ikkita inkor bor.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda sinf rasmini hozir kuzatayotgandek yozing: odamlar, ishlar va ikki inkor.
writing.model: We are painting a picture for our school corridor. I am drawing a river across the middle. My friend is painting small trees beside it. Two students are colouring the sky. Our teacher is holding a tray of paint. She isn't drawing today. Aziz is washing the brushes in a bucket. He isn't cleaning the floor. Some younger children are watching us from the door. We are working carefully, but there is blue paint on my elbow. Our picture is becoming a little garden inside the school.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Kamida beshta am/is/are + -ing gapi bor.
Ikki inkor matndagi vaziyatga mos.

teacherNote: Oldindan: mural — devoriy rasm, corridor — yo‘lak, mechanic — mexanik. Readingni muzlatilgan kadr sifatida tasvirlang; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib harakatlarni belgilang. Sekin o‘quvchiga be + fe’l-ing kartalari; ilg‘orga ikki kuzatuvni inkorga aylantirish. Scaffold: although — garchi tayyor bog‘lovchi; Is the bus coming? hozircha tushunish savoli, keyingi darsda faol o‘tiladi.

objective: Present Continuous bilan yes/no va wh-savollar tuzaman.

reading.title: The Live Kitchen Screen
reading.text: Our school kitchen has a live screen today. What is the chef making? She is making vegetable soup. Is her assistant cutting carrots? No, he is cutting onions. Why is the chef smiling? A carrot has two long legs. It looks like a tiny dancer. Who is holding the camera? Our science teacher is holding it. The students are watching in the hall. They are learning about food without crowding the kitchen.

questions.prompt: What is the chef making? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “She is making vegetable soup” — sabzavotli sho‘rva.

questions.prompt: What is the assistant cutting? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “He is cutting onions” — piyoz to‘g‘rayapti.

questions.prompt: Who is holding the camera? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Our science teacher is holding it” — tabiiy fan o‘qituvchisi.

listening.title: The Noisy Upstairs Room
listening.text:
Tenant: What are you moving upstairs?
Neighbour: We are moving a table. Are we making too much noise?
Tenant: A little. Are you building a new room?
Neighbour: No. We are preparing for a birthday dinner.
Tenant: Where are you putting the table?
Neighbour: By the window. My brother is carrying the chairs.
Tenant: Why is he singing?
Neighbour: He is testing the birthday song. The furniture is his first audience!

questions.prompt: What are the neighbours moving? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “We are moving a table” — stol ko‘chiryapti.

questions.prompt: What are they preparing for? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Preparing for a birthday dinner” — tug‘ilgan kun ovqati.

questions.prompt: Where are they putting the table? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “By the window” — deraza yoniga.

speaking.prompt: 60–75 soniyada oshxona jonli efiri intervyusini o‘ynang: uch wh-savol va bitta yes/no savol bering.
success: Be egadan oldin to‘g‘ri qo‘yiladi.
What/where/why dan kamida ikkitasi bor.
Javoblarda -ing harakat savolga mos.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda tug‘ilgan kun tayyorgarligi haqida savol-javobli xabar yozing.
writing.model: What are we doing in the dining room? We are preparing for Grandma's birthday. Are we moving the sofa? No, we are moving the table. My brother is carrying chairs from the kitchen. Where are we putting the cake? We are putting it on the small table by the window. Mum is bringing plates. Why is Dad holding a wooden spoon? He is practising a funny song, and the spoon is his microphone. Grandma is waiting in the garden. We are keeping the room quiet for one more minute.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Kamida uch Present Continuous savoli va javobi bor.
Har savolda be + ega + -ing tartibi to‘g‘ri.

teacherNote: Oldindan: onion — piyoz, tenant — ijarachi, audience — tomoshabinlar. Readingdagi savolga aniq gapni ulang; dialogni ikki bor o‘qib harakat va sababni ajrating. Sekin o‘quvchiga savol kartalari; ilg‘orga javobdan yangi why savoli. Scaffold: without crowding — tiqilinch qilmasdan va for one more minute — yana bir daqiqa tayyor birikmalar.

objective: Present Continuous qisqa javoblari va making/running/lying kabi -ing imlosini qo‘llayman.

reading.title: Sports Day Snapshots
reading.text: The sports field is busy. Are the runners running? Yes, they are. Is our coach sitting? No, she isn't. She is clapping near the line. Two children are tying their shoes. A parent is making a sign for the team. One boy is lying on a picnic blanket, but he isn't sleeping. He is watching a beetle. The beetle is winning its own tiny race across his sandwich box.

questions.prompt: What is the coach doing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “She is clapping near the line” — qarsak chalmoqda.

questions.prompt: What are two children tying? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Tying their shoes” — oyoq kiyim bog‘ichlarini bog‘lamoqda.

questions.prompt: What is the boy watching? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “He is watching a beetle” — qo‘ng‘izni kuzatyapti.

listening.title: The Model Workshop
listening.text:
Teacher: Are you making a boat, Lola?
Lola: Yes, I am. I am cutting paper for the sail.
Teacher: Is Akmal using glue?
Lola: No, he isn't. He is tying string around his model.
Teacher: Are the twins sitting at the back?
Lola: Yes, they are. They are planning a bridge.
Teacher: And your little brother?
Lola: He is lying on the carpet and drawing a river. Our boats finally have somewhere to go!

questions.prompt: What is Lola making? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Are you making a boat? … Yes” — qayiq.

questions.prompt: Is Akmal using glue? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “No, he isn't” — yelim ishlatmayapti.

questions.prompt: What are the twins planning? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “They are planning a bridge” — ko‘prik rejalashtiryapti.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqa sport kuni suratini tasvirlang. Sherik uch yes/no savol bersin, siz qisqa javob bering.
success: Uchta qisqa javob ega va be ga mos.
Running/sitting kabi undoshi ikkilangan shakl aytiladi.
Making yoki lying/tying bilan bitta harakat tasvirlanadi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda sport maydonidagi surat ostiga izoh yozing; ikki qisqa savol-javob ham bo‘lsin.
writing.model: This is our school sports day. Two runners are running towards the finish line. Our coach is clapping beside them. Is she sitting down? No, she isn't. My friend is tying his shoes near the bench. Two parents are making a large sign for our team. Are the younger children sleeping on the blanket? No, they aren't. They are lying on their stomachs and watching a beetle. I am taking a photo of the race. There are two races in my picture: the students' race and the beetle's race.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Running, making va tying/lying imlosi to‘g‘ri.
Ikki qisqa javob asosiy savolga mos.

teacherNote: Oldindan: clap — qarsak chalmoq, beetle — qo‘ng‘iz, sail — yelkan. Readingda -ing shakllarini uch imlo guruhiga ajrating; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib qisqa javoblarni qayd eting. Sekin o‘quvchiga run→running va lie→lying kartalari; ilg‘orga cut/sit/plan misollarini mustaqil yasash. Talaffuz mashqida qo‘sh undoshni ortiqcha cho‘zdirish shart emas, imlosiga e’tibor qarating.

objective: Hozirgi harakat va shu davrdagi vaqtinchalik vaziyatni Present Continuous orqali farqlayman.

reading.title: A Temporary Classroom
reading.text: This week, our class is studying in the library. Workers are repairing our classroom floor. Today we are sitting between the geography and history shelves. Our teacher is using a small whiteboard. We are keeping our voices low. I am borrowing my cousin's desk lamp this week because the corner is dark. The librarian is joining our lesson now. She is learning our class song, but we are singing it very quietly.

questions.prompt: Where is the class studying this week? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “This week … in the library” — bu hafta kutubxonada.

questions.prompt: What are workers repairing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Repairing our classroom floor” — sinf polini.

questions.prompt: Whose lamp is the narrator borrowing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “My cousin's desk lamp” — amakivachcha/xolavachchasining lampasi.

listening.title: Staying with an Aunt
listening.text:
Friend: Are you living with your aunt now, Timur?
Timur: Just this month. Our family is painting our flat.
Friend: What are you doing at the moment?
Timur: I am helping her in the garden. We are planting beans.
Friend: Is your brother staying there too?
Timur: Yes. He is sleeping in the small room this month. Right now, he is carrying water. My aunt's cat is supervising from a comfortable chair.

questions.prompt: How long is Timur staying with his aunt? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Just this month” — faqat shu oy.

questions.prompt: What are they planting now? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “We are planting beans” — loviya ekishyapti.

questions.prompt: What is his brother doing right now? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Right now, he is carrying water” — suv tashiyapti.

speaking.prompt: 60–75 soniyada vaqtinchalik sinf haqida xabar bering: this week bilan ikki holat, now bilan ikki harakat.
success: This week/month bilan vaqtinchalik vaziyat aytiladi.
Now/right now bilan kuzatilayotgan harakat bor.
To‘rtta be + -ing tuzilmasi to‘g‘ri.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda bir hafta boshqa xonada o‘qiyotgan sinf haqida do‘stingizga xabar yozing.
writing.model: This week, we are studying in the school library. Workers are repairing our classroom floor. We are using the tables near the history shelves. Our teacher is carrying her books here every morning this week. Right now, she is drawing a map on a small whiteboard. I am sitting beside my best friend. We are speaking quietly because other people are reading. Our class is keeping its bags under the tables. The librarian is helping us with our project today. Our temporary classroom is full of interesting books.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Vaqtinchalik davr va ayni payt aniq ajratilgan.
Kamida besh Present Continuous gapi bor.

teacherNote: Oldindan: temporary — vaqtinchalik, repair — ta’mirlamoq, bean — loviya. Readingda this week va now ni ikki ustunga ajrating; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib davr va hozirgi ishni topdiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga vaqt chizig‘i; ilg‘orga bir harakatni now/this month kontekstlarida ishlatish. Supervising — nazorat qilmoqda so‘zini mushukning kulgili roli orqali tushuntiring.

objective: Odat, hozirgi jarayon, o‘zgarish va holat fe’llarini farqlayman.

reading.title: The Greener Street
reading.text: Our street is changing. More neighbours are growing plants on their balconies. I usually walk past grey walls, but this month I am seeing flowers everywhere. Our neighbour owns a small shop. He is putting pots by the door today. He believes plants make people happy. I agree with him. The street is becoming colourful. My brother wants a tree on our balcony, but Mum knows our balcony is too small.

questions.prompt: What are more neighbours growing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “More neighbours are growing plants” — o‘simliklar.

questions.prompt: Where is the shop owner putting pots today? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Putting pots by the door today” — eshik yoniga.

questions.prompt: What does the brother want? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “My brother wants a tree on our balcony” — daraxt istaydi.

listening.title: The Cafe's New Habit
listening.text:
Customer: You usually serve drinks in paper cups. Why are you using mugs today?
Owner: We are reducing our waste. More customers are bringing their own cups too.
Customer: I like that idea. I don't need a paper cup.
Owner: Our assistant is washing the mugs now. He usually works at the till.
Customer: Does he enjoy washing up?
Owner: He prefers the till, but he understands the plan. Our sink is becoming a very busy place.

questions.prompt: What does the cafe usually use? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Usually serve drinks in paper cups” — qog‘oz stakan.

questions.prompt: What is the assistant doing now? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Washing the mugs now” — krujkalarni yuvmoqda.

questions.prompt: Where does the assistant prefer working? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “He prefers the till” — kassani afzal ko‘radi.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqada kafe o‘zgarishini tushuntiring: odatiy holat, bugungi ish va fikringizni ayting.
success: Usually bilan Present Simple ishlatiladi.
Now/today bilan Continuous ishlatiladi.
Like/know/want kabi holat fe’li keraksiz -ing olmaydi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda mahallangizdagi bir ijobiy o‘zgarishni odatlaringiz bilan bog‘lab yozing.
writing.model: Our street is becoming greener. People usually keep plants inside their homes, but this month many neighbours are putting pots outside. I walk to school along this street every day. I like the new flowers, and I know several neighbours by name. Today, the shop owner is watering his plants near the door. He usually opens his shop at nine. He believes a friendly street is good for everyone. My brother wants a huge tree for our balcony. I understand his idea, but our balcony needs a small plant.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Odat va o‘zgarish uchun ikki zamon to‘g‘ri ajratilgan.
Kamida uch holat fe’li Simple shaklida.

teacherNote: Oldindan: balcony — balkon, waste — chiqindi, till — kassa. Readingda odat/o‘zgarish/fikrni uch rangda belgilang; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib usually/now juftlarini topdiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga like/know/want banki; ilg‘orga o‘zgarishni bir dalil bilan asoslash. Scaffold: am seeing bu yerda ko‘zga qayta-qayta tashlanayotgan vaqtinchalik tajriba; sodda qoida uchun asosiy ishlab chiqarishda see ni Simple bilan qo‘llang.

objective: 7-haftada o‘tilgan Continuous shakllarini Simple bilan birgalikda mustaqil qo‘llayman.

reading.title: Open Day behind the Scenes
reading.text: Our school holds an open day every year. Today, students are showing visitors their projects. I usually work in the science room, but now I am guiding parents through the garden. Two friends are testing a small water wheel. It isn't turning fast because the water flow is weak. Our teacher is carrying a bucket. She knows a simple solution. The parents are watching, and one little child is cheering for the wheel.

questions.prompt: What is the narrator doing now? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Now I am guiding parents through the garden” — ota-onalarni bog‘da olib yurmoqda.

questions.prompt: Why is the wheel not turning fast? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
answers: because the water flow is weak
questions.explanation: “Because the water flow is weak” — suv oqimi kuchsiz.

questions.prompt: What is the teacher carrying? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Our teacher is carrying a bucket” — chelak.

listening.title: The Station Piano
listening.text:
Presenter: What are you playing today, Mariam?
Mariam: A simple folk song. I usually practise at home, but this week I am playing at the station.
Presenter: Are people stopping to listen?
Mariam: Yes, they are. A little boy is dancing by his suitcase.
Presenter: Do you know him?
Mariam: No, I don't. His father is filming him. I love this piano. It gives waiting passengers something cheerful.
Presenter: The station has its own tiny concert now.

questions.prompt: Where does Mariam usually practise? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I usually practise at home” — odatda uyda.

questions.prompt: What is the boy doing? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “A little boy is dancing” — bola raqsga tushmoqda.

questions.prompt: Does Mariam know the boy? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: Mariam “No, I don't” deb javob beradi — u bolani tanimaydi.

speaking.prompt: 60–75 soniyada ochiq eshiklar kunidan jonli xabar bering. Odatni hozirgi ishga solishtiring va sherik savoliga javob bering.
success: Odat uchun Simple, hozir uchun Continuous to‘g‘ri.
Bitta inkor va bitta qisqa javob bor.
Know/like/want dan biri Simple shaklida.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda stansiyadagi kichik konsertni kuzatayotgan do‘stingiz nomidan xabar yozing.
writing.model: I am waiting at the station with my father. A woman is playing a folk song on the piano. She usually practises at home, but this week she is playing here. Several passengers are standing near her. A little boy is dancing beside his suitcase. His father is filming him. Are people enjoying the music? Yes, they are. I don't know the musician, but I like her song. Our train isn't here yet. We usually read while we wait. Today, we are listening to a free concert.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Odat va vaqtinchalik ishlar aniq.
Bir Continuous savol-javobi va bir Simple inkori bor.

teacherNote: Oldindan: water wheel — suv g‘ildiragi, flow — oqim, folk song — xalq qo‘shig‘i. 6-kun readingda hozir/odatni mustaqil ajrating; listeningni ikki marta o‘qib dalillarni qayd eting. Sekin o‘quvchiga ikki vaqt ustuni; ilg‘orga stansiyadagi uchinchi shaxs nuqtayi nazaridan xabar. Bu ichki mashq; ravonlikdan tashqari ma’no va shaklga aniq fikr bering.

objective: What/which, who/whose va why/how savollarini maqsadga mos tanlayman.

reading.title: Choosing the Club Poster
reading.text: Our club needs a poster. What is the event? It is a neighbourhood picnic. Which design do we prefer, the green one or the blue one? We prefer the green one. Who is drawing it? Our friend Dilfuza is drawing it. Whose camera are we using? We are using her brother's camera. Why is there a giant spoon in the picture? It represents our shared meal. How are we printing the posters? On the school printer.

questions.prompt: Which design do they prefer? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “We prefer the green one” — yashil dizayn.

questions.prompt: Whose camera are they using? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Her brother's camera” — Dilfuzaning akasi/ukasining kamerasi.

questions.prompt: How are they printing the posters? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “On the school printer” — maktab printerida.

listening.title: Finding a Chess Partner
listening.text:
Organiser: What game do you enjoy, Pavel?
Pavel: Chess. Which table is for beginners, this one or that one?
Organiser: This one. Who is your partner?
Pavel: My cousin. Whose clock is on the table?
Organiser: It's mine.
Pavel: Why do we need it?
Organiser: It measures each player's time.
Pavel: How do we start?
Organiser: Move a piece, then press the clock. The clock is strict, but your cousin is friendly!

questions.prompt: Which table is for beginners? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “This one” — tashkilotchi yaqin stolni ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Who owns the clock? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: Tashkilotchi “It's mine” deydi.

questions.prompt: What should Pavel do after moving a piece? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Move a piece, then press the clock” — keyin soatni bosadi.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqada afisha rejasi bo‘yicha suhbat qiling: what/which va who/whose farqini amalda ko‘rsating.
success: Which aniq ikki variantga oid.
Who odamni, whose egani so‘raydi.
Why sabab, how usul haqidagi javob oladi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda klub afishasi uchun savol-javobli reja yozing.
writing.model: What is our event? It is a picnic for our neighbours. Which poster do we like, the green one or the yellow one? We like the yellow one because it looks sunny. Who is drawing the main picture? Dilfuza is drawing a large picnic basket. Whose camera are we using? We are using my brother's camera for a group photo. Why do we need a photo? It introduces our team. How are we sharing the poster? We are putting copies in the library and near the school gate.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Olti savol so‘zi maqsadga mos ishlatilgan.
Har bir savolga aniq mos javob berilgan.

teacherNote: Oldindan: design — dizayn, represent — ifodalamoq, measure — o‘lchamoq. Readingda savollarni ma’lumot turiga ajrating; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib kim/kimniki farqini tekshiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga o‘zbekcha ma’no kartalari; ilg‘orga bitta javobga ikki xil savol tuzdiring. Move … then press buyruqlari oldingi haftadan qaytariladi.

objective: Yosh, masofa, davomiylik va miqdorni so‘rayman, Who + fe’l ega savolini tuzaman.

reading.title: The Old Footbridge
reading.text: Our village footbridge is eighty years old. It is fifty metres from the bus stop. The walk across it takes two minutes. How many people use it each day? About sixty people use it. How much does it cost to cross? Nothing; it is free. Who checks the bridge? A council worker checks it every Monday. Our oldest neighbour calls it the young bridge. She is ninety, so she has a point.

questions.prompt: How old is the bridge? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Eighty years old” — sakson yoshda.

questions.prompt: How far is it from the bus stop? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Fifty metres from the bus stop” — ellik metr.

questions.prompt: Who checks it? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “A council worker checks it” — mahalliy idora xodimi.

listening.title: Joining the Pottery Session
listening.text:
Caller: How long is the pottery session?
Teacher: Ninety minutes.
Caller: How many students are in each group?
Teacher: Eight. Everyone has a work space.
Caller: How much clay do we use?
Teacher: About half a kilo each.
Caller: Who brings the tools?
Teacher: I bring them. You bring an apron.
Caller: How old is your youngest student?
Teacher: Seven. Her bowls are small, but her ideas are enormous.

questions.prompt: How long is the session? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Ninety minutes” — to‘qson daqiqa.

questions.prompt: How many students are in a group? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Eight” — guruhda sakkiz kishi.

questions.prompt: Who brings the tools? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: O‘qituvchi “I bring them” deydi — asboblarni u keltiradi.

speaking.prompt: 60–75 soniyada mahalladagi ko‘prik yoki kurs haqida ma’lumot so‘rang: yosh, masofa yoki vaqt, son va mas’ul kishi.
success: How old/long/far dan ikkitasi mos.
How much/how many sanalishga mos.
Who + fe’l savolida ortiqcha do ishlatilmaydi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda kulolchilik darsi uchun ma’lumot sahifasini savol-javob bilan yozing.
writing.model: How long is our pottery class? It lasts ninety minutes. How many students are in the group? There are eight students, and each student has a table space. How much clay does each person use? About half a kilo. Who brings the tools? Our teacher brings them in a large box. Students bring their own aprons. How old is the youngest student? She is seven. She makes tiny bowls for her toy animals. The class is friendly, and beginners are welcome. Your first bowl doesn't need to be perfect.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Vaqt, son va miqdor aniq ko‘rsatilgan.
Bitta to‘g‘ri ega savoli va javobi bor.

teacherNote: Oldindan: footbridge — piyodalar ko‘prigi, pottery — kulolchilik, clay — loy. Readingdagi o‘lchovlarni birliklari bilan yozdiring; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib sonlarni tekshiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga years/metres/minutes ustunlari; ilg‘orga who checks va what does he check farqini ayttiring. Has a point — gapida jon bor iborasini tayyor ma’no sifatida tushuntiring.

objective: To‘ldiruvchi savollari va joy predloglari orqali odam-buyumlarni topaman.

reading.title: The Museum Desk Puzzle
reading.text: Our museum guide keeps the tickets in a drawer. She puts the map on the desk. A small clock is between the map and a lamp. What does she check first each morning? She checks the visitor list. Who does she call after that? She calls the caretaker. His office is behind the gift shop. Today, her pen is under the visitor book. The guide knows every ancient object, but her pen is a daily mystery.

questions.prompt: What does the guide check first? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “She checks the visitor list” — tashrifchilar ro‘yxati.

questions.prompt: Who does she call? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “She calls the caretaker” — xo‘jalik xodimi.

questions.prompt: Where is her pen today? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Her pen is under the visitor book” — tashrif daftarining ostida.

listening.title: The Rehearsal Room
listening.text:
Director: Who do you need for this scene?
Actor: I need Madina. Where is she?
Director: She is at the piano. What are you looking for?
Actor: My script. Is it on the chair?
Director: No. It is in the bag between the two chairs.
Actor: The red bag?
Director: Yes. Your hat is behind the piano too.
Actor: My things know their places. I am the only confused person here!

questions.prompt: Who does the actor need? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “I need Madina” — Madina kerak.

questions.prompt: Where is the script? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
answers: in the bag between the chairs
questions.explanation: “It is in the bag between the two chairs” joyni bildiradi; “The red bag?” savoliga “Yes” javobi sumkaning qizilligini tasdiqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Where is the hat? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Your hat is behind the piano” — pianino orqasida.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqa muzey stolidagi buyumlarni topish o‘yinini o‘ynang: ikki to‘ldiruvchi savoli va uch joy javobi.
success: What/Who does …? shakli to‘g‘ri.
In/on/at dan ikkitasi mos.
Under/behind/between bilan aniq joy aytiladi.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda yangi muzey xodimiga ish joyini tushuntiruvchi savol-javob yozing.
writing.model: What does our guide check every morning? She checks the visitor list in the blue folder. Who does she call after that? She calls the caretaker. His office is behind the gift shop. The tickets are in the drawer under the desk. The map is on the desk, between the clock and the lamp. Our guide meets visitors at the front door. Where does she keep her pen? It is usually in her pocket, but today it is under the visitor book. The desk has a place for everything.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Kamida ikki to‘ldiruvchi savoli bor.
To‘rtta joy birikmasi bir-biriga zid emas.

teacherNote: Oldindan: drawer — tortma, caretaker — xo‘jalik xodimi, script — sahna matni. Readingdan stol chizmasini tuzing; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib buyumlarni qo‘ying. Sekin o‘quvchiga predlog rasm kartalari; ilg‘orga who calls/who does she call juftini izohlash. Looking for — qidirmoq tayyor birikma sifatida ko‘rsatiladi.

objective: Harakat va vaqt predloglari bilan yo‘l hamda kun tartibini aniq tushuntiraman.

reading.title: The Morning Market Route
reading.text: On Saturdays, I walk to the market with my aunt. We leave at eight in the morning. We go across the bridge and into the covered market. My aunt buys vegetables before breakfast. I carry the empty bags until we reach her favourite stall. After shopping, we walk out of the market and sit in the park. Our bags are full, but my aunt always finds space for one more bunch of herbs.

questions.prompt: When do they leave? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “We leave at eight in the morning” — ertalab sakkizda.

questions.prompt: What do they cross? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “We go across the bridge” — ko‘prikdan o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Where do they sit after shopping? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “After shopping … sit in the park” — bog‘da.

listening.title: The Swimming Lesson Route
listening.text:
Coach: Our lesson is on Tuesday at four. Come to the side entrance.
Parent: Do we go into the changing room first?
Coach: Yes. Walk across the hall, then go into the room on the left. Wait there until four.
Parent: And after the lesson?
Coach: Meet your child outside the changing room. The lesson ends at five.
Parent: Good. My son packs his goggles before school. He is ready hours before the water is!

questions.prompt: On which day is the lesson? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “On Tuesday at four” — seshanba.

questions.prompt: What time does it end? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “The lesson ends at five” — beshda.

questions.prompt: Where should parents meet children afterwards? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Outside the changing room” — kiyinish xonasining tashqarisida.

speaking.prompt: 60–75 soniyada bozorga borish yo‘lingiz va jadvalingizni ayting: harakat, boshlanish va keyingi ish.
success: To/into/out of/across dan uchtasi ishlatiladi.
On va at vaqtga mos.
Before/after/until dan ikkitasi ma’noga mos.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda birinchi marta suzish darsiga keladigan oilaga yo‘l va vaqtni tushuntiring.
writing.model: The swimming lesson is on Tuesday at four in the afternoon. Come to the side entrance before the lesson. Walk across the hall and go into the changing room on the left. Children wait there until four. The coach meets them at the door. Parents wait in the cafe during the lesson. After swimming, meet your child outside the changing room. The lesson ends at five. Bring a towel and goggles. Put dry clothes in a separate bag. A warm jumper is useful after an hour in the pool.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Yo‘lning uch bosqichi aniq.
On/at va before/after/until bilan vaqt izchil.

teacherNote: Oldindan: stall — rasta, entrance — kirish, goggles — suzish ko‘zoynagi. Reading yo‘lini strelkalar bilan chizing; listeningni ikki marta o‘qib vaqt–joyni yozdiring. Sekin o‘quvchiga yo‘l sxemasi; ilg‘orga teskari yo‘lni izohlash. Scaffold: during the lesson modelda tayyor birikma; ertaga tizimli ko‘riladi.

objective: From…to, during/for va ravishlar yordamida ishning qayerda, qanday, qachon bajarilishini aytaman.

reading.title: The Practice Room Agreement
reading.text: Our music group uses the community room from six to seven on Fridays. We practise there quietly for the first ten minutes. During the session, our leader listens carefully and gives advice. Sami plays the drums well, but he sometimes plays too loudly. We work hard on the final song. After practice, we carry the chairs outside carefully. The neighbours wave from their windows. Our quiet ending is their favourite part of the concert.

questions.prompt: When does the group use the room on Fridays? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “From six to seven on Fridays” — oltidan yettigacha.

questions.prompt: For how long do they practise quietly at first? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “For the first ten minutes” — dastlabki o‘n daqiqa.

questions.prompt: Who plays the drums well? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Sami plays the drums well” — Sami.

listening.title: The Table Tennis Schedule
listening.text:
Coach: We train here from five to six on Mondays.
New player: How long do we warm up?
Coach: For ten minutes. Walk slowly at first, then move quickly between the markers.
New player: Do we talk during matches?
Coach: Not during a point. Listen carefully between games. Your partner plays well, so watch her feet.
New player: I work hard, but I don't move fast yet.
Coach: That's fine. Good practice matters more than noisy shoes.

questions.prompt: When is training on Mondays? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “From five to six on Mondays” — beshdan oltigacha.

questions.prompt: How long is the warm-up? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “For ten minutes” — o‘n daqiqa.

questions.prompt: What should the new player watch? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Watch her feet” — sherikning oyoq harakatlari.

speaking.prompt: Bir daqiqada musiqa yoki sport mashqi jadvalini ayting: vaqt oralig‘i, davomiylik, joy va qanday bajarish.
success: From…to va for ma’nosi farqlangan.
During dan keyin voqea nomi aytiladi.
Well/hard/fast dan biri va ikkita -ly ravishi bor.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda yangi musiqa a’zosi uchun mashq tartibini yozing.
writing.model: We practise in the community room from six to seven on Fridays. We play quietly for the first ten minutes. During this time, our leader listens carefully to each instrument. Sami plays the drums well, and Lola sings clearly. We work hard on one song before the break. After the break, we play the whole song together. Put your instrument in its case carefully after practice. Carry the chairs outside slowly at seven. The neighbours are friendly, and we respect their quiet evening. Our group makes music, not a thunderstorm.
success: 80–100 so‘z yozilgan.
Vaqt oralig‘i va davomiylik aniq.
Ravishlar harakatni to‘g‘ri tavsiflaydi; hard va hardly almashtirilmagan.

teacherNote: Oldindan: drum — baraban, warm up — badan qizdirmoq, marker — belgi. Readingda vaqt ifodalarini ajrating; listeningni ikki bor o‘qib tartibni tiklang. Sekin o‘quvchiga during + voqea / for + muddat qolipi; ilg‘orga hard/hardly ma’no farqini tarjimasiz misol bilan ko‘rsatish. Matters more than iborasi mazmun uchun, qiyoslash qoidasi hali talab qilinmaydi.

objective: 8-haftadagi savol, joy, harakat, vaqt va ravishlarni bir vaziyatda mustaqil birlashtiraman.

reading.title: The Community Treasure Walk
reading.text: Our treasure walk starts at the library on Sunday at ten. Teams walk across the square and into the park. Who writes the clues? Our librarian writes them. How long does the walk take? About forty minutes. Each team follows the map carefully. The last clue is under a bench between two trees. The treasure is a box of bookmarks. Nobody becomes rich, but everyone leaves with a good reason to read.

questions.prompt: Who writes the clues? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Our librarian writes them” — kutubxonachi.

questions.prompt: How long does the walk take? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “About forty minutes” — taxminan qirq daqiqa.

questions.prompt: What is the treasure? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “The treasure is a box of bookmarks” — xatcho‘plar qutisi.

listening.title: The Museum Volunteer Briefing
listening.text:
Coordinator: Which entrance do visitors use, the front or the side?
Volunteer: The front entrance. Who meets them?
Coordinator: I do. You check tickets at the desk from ten to twelve.
Volunteer: Where do I put their bags?
Coordinator: In the cupboard behind you. Speak clearly and show each visitor the map.
Volunteer: How long is the tour?
Coordinator: Forty minutes. During the tour, keep the hall quiet. Our oldest exhibit is a clock, and it needs no extra ticking!

questions.prompt: Which entrance do visitors use? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “The front entrance” — oldingi kirish.

questions.prompt: When does the volunteer check tickets? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “From ten to twelve” — o‘ndan o‘n ikkigacha.

questions.prompt: Where should bags go? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “In the cupboard behind you” — ko‘ngilli orqasidagi shkaf.

speaking.prompt: 75 soniyada xazina sayrini tushuntiring; sherik vaqt, yo‘l va mas’ul kishi haqida uch savol bersin.
success: Ega va to‘ldiruvchi savoli farqlanadi.
Ikki harakat yoki joy predlogi to‘g‘ri.
Aniq vaqt, davomiylik va bitta ravish bor.

writing.prompt: 80–100 so‘zda yangi jamoa uchun xazina sayri yo‘riqnomasini yozing.
writing.model: Our treasure walk starts at the library on Sunday at ten. Who writes the clues? Our librarian writes them. Walk across the square and go into the park. Read each clue carefully before you move. How long does the walk take? About forty minutes. Stay with your team during the walk. The final clue is under a bench between two trees. Open the small box beside it. There are bookmarks inside for every team member. The treasure is simple, but the walk gives us time together and a new story.
success: 80–100 so‘z bor.
Yo‘l, vaqt va yakuniy joy izchil.
Ikki savol-javob va ravishli ko‘rsatma to‘g‘ri.

reading.title: The Silent Birthday
reading.text: Yesterday was my grandfather's birthday. Our family was in the garden, but Grandfather wasn't there at first. He was in the kitchen with a large bowl of cherries. The garden was quiet because our surprise was a silent party. There were paper messages on every chair. My message was 'You are wonderful!' My little brother's message was only a picture of a cake. He is six, and long words are difficult for him. Grandfather was very happy with the messages. His eyes were wet, but he wasn't sad. The cake was small and slightly crooked. My brother was proud of it. At the end, everyone was noisy again. A silent party is lovely, but a family of twelve isn't silent for long.

listening.title: A Wet Museum Visit

Guide: Hello, Nargiza. Was your school trip good yesterday?
Nargiza: Yes, it was. The dinosaur room was wonderful.
Guide: Were all your classmates there?
Nargiza: No, they weren't. Aziz was at home with a cold. There were nineteen of us.
Guide: Was the weather nice?
Nargiza: No. Our shoes were wet, but the museum was warm. My socks were two different colours, so everyone was cheerful.

Nargiza: No, she wasn't. She was interested in a tiny dinosaur egg.

Nargiza: The cafe wasn't open. Our sandwiches were in our bags, so that wasn't a problem. My sandwich was enormous. The dinosaur was big, but my lunch was impressive too.

reading.text: Last Saturday our reading club was inside an old bus. The bus was in the school yard, and its wheels were still on it. There was a long shelf above the seats. Its name was Motor, and its quiet breathing was our background music. There were eight readers at the meeting. Everyone was comfortable, although the leader's seat was a little too high for her feet.

listening.title: After the Costume Show
listening.text:
Mum: Where were you at four yesterday, Jasur?
Jasur: I was behind the school stage. There was a costume show.
Mum: Who was with you?
Jasur: My friend Bek was there. He was a tree, and I was a cloud.
Mum: Were your costumes heavy?
Jasur: Mine wasn't. Bek's was, because there were real branches on it.
Mum: How many people were in the audience?
Jasur: There were thirty parents. There was a baby in the front row too.
Mum: Was the baby quiet?
Jasur: Yes, she was. The adults were noisy!
Mum: Why was your face blue?
Jasur: There was blue paint inside my cloud. My face was the sky, apparently. Our art teacher was very pleased with the whole picture, but my nose was cold. Mum: That was certainly a colourful school afternoon.

reading.text: Our class opened a small swap market on Friday. There wasn't a cash box, because nobody needed money. People brought useful things from home and exchanged them. I brought a puzzle and took a green notebook. My friend Lola carried a huge bag into the hall. Everyone expected toys, but she opened the bag and showed us twelve clean plant pots. Her grandmother gave them to her. There weren't any plants inside, so our science teacher added seeds to each pot. A boy near the door asked, 'Were there any rules?' There was one important rule: every object was clean and safe. We checked the tables at five and counted twenty successful swaps. Lola went home with a chess set. Her empty bag looked very relieved.

listening.title: The Missing Picnic Bench
listening.text:
Dilshod: Was there a bench near the river yesterday?
Saida: No, there wasn't. We walked to the usual place, but there weren't any seats there.

reading.title: A Robot with a Brush
reading.text: Yesterday our technology club tested a painting robot. We attached a brush to a small toy car and placed paper on the floor. The car moved slowly and painted a blue line. It stopped near my shoe, but it didn't touch it. We wanted a picture of a river. Unfortunately, the second line looked like a very tired snake. Our teacher didn't laugh at the picture. She asked, 'Did you plan the turns?' We didn't plan them. We only pressed the forward button and hoped for art. Then we marked three stopping points on the paper and tried again. This time the river looked good. We cleaned the wheels, washed the brush and displayed our picture. The robot didn't sign its work, so we added all our names.

Baker: Hello, this is the bakery. Did you collect the birthday cake this morning?

reading.title: The Umbrella Race
reading.text: Two days ago our street held an umbrella race. It wasn't a running race. Each team decorated an umbrella and walked slowly across the square. My sister and I made a yellow sun on ours. We started at eleven, just before a light shower. Other teams carried fish, flowers and even a tiny paper castle above their heads. Who won the prize? A quiet man with a plain black umbrella won it. He put a clear plastic pocket on top and filled it with colourful autumn leaves. The judges loved the idea. The prize was a blue watering can, which made everyone laugh in the rain. We didn't win, but our yellow sun stayed bright. We were cold at the end, so we went home for hot tea.

Our guide wrote down the incident in the visitors' book, beside our ordinary names.

listening.title: A Station Piano
listening.text:
Friend: Have you ever played a public piano, Iroda?
Iroda: No, I haven't. I have only played at home and at school.
Friend: There is one in the station hall. The previous player has just left.
Iroda: I have never played with strangers around me. What about you?
Friend: Yes, I have. I played here last month while I was waiting for my train.
Iroda: What did people do?
Friend: Two children danced, and a man tapped his suitcase. Nobody expected a concert.
Iroda: All right. I have just remembered a short song from my first music book.
Friend: Perfect. Our train hasn't arrived, so there is time.
Iroda: Please stand nearby. I don't need an audience, just one friendly face.
Friend: Of course. And my suitcase is available as a drum, but only with your permission.

We searched the building for ten minutes before the cook opened the cupboard. The cake was perfect, and the candles were beside it. The host thanked everyone and placed the flowers somewhere else. listening.title: Before the Weather Balloon Launch
listening.text:
Leader: Why did we delay the balloon launch yesterday?
Student: We hadn't checked the wind direction before we carried the balloon outside.
Leader: Had you attached the camera?
Student: Yes, we had. But we hadn't switched it on.
Leader: What had the other team prepared?
Student: They had prepared the tracking phone and written the emergency contact number on the box.
Leader: Had anyone tested the battery?
Student: No, nobody had. We checked it during the delay, and it was nearly empty.
Leader: So the delay helped us.
Student: Definitely. We changed the battery and checked everything again. The balloon rose at eleven instead of ten.
Leader: Did the camera work?
Student: Yes. The first picture showed your nose because you were looking straight into it. The later pictures showed the fields, which was our actual aim.

reading.title: The Painter's Blue Hands
reading.text: When I visited my neighbour's workshop yesterday, her hands were blue and the floor was covered with newspaper. She had been painting a wooden cupboard for three hours. She hadn't been using gloves because she couldn't find a pair small enough for her hands. Had she finished the whole cupboard? No, she hadn't. Her dog watched from the doorway and kept a careful distance from the paint. We put a clean sheet under the shelves and made tea. By then, my hands were blue too. The cupboard had gained colour, and I had gained an unexpected afternoon project.

reading.text: Our drama teacher found six students asleep on chairs after lunch. Had they been avoiding rehearsal? No, they hadn't. They had been rehearsing a difficult scene since nine that morning. reading.title: The Parcel-Packing Trial
reading.text: Our school shop compared two ways of packing books for delivery. The first group used loose paper and ordinary tape. The second group used folded cardboard corners. Our shop leader suggested another practice round before choosing a method. Fast packing is useful, but books need to arrive safely. The cardboard corners looked rather like tiny hats, so we called the trial 'Fashion Week for Novels'.

reading.title: Two Tents and One Decision
reading.text: Our hiking group inspected two tents before a weekend trip. Both of them were clean, but neither was perfect. The green tent had enough space for three people, although it was too heavy for our youngest members to carry. The orange tent was light, but there was little room for bags inside. We had a little money left in the equipment budget, enough for one waterproof storage cover. Most of the group preferred the orange tent with bags outside under that cover. Two members preferred the green one because they wanted everything indoors. All of us agreed that either tent was safe in mild weather. None of the poles were damaged. Finally, we chose the orange tent and the cover. Our leader reminded us that dry socks matter more than a bedroom large enough for a dance party.

reading.text: Our student council compared three donated school bags before choosing a model for next year's collection. She still couldn't dive, but that wasn't the teacher's first goal. Today she takes her grandchildren swimming and understands their nervousness. She keeps her old swimming cap in a drawer. It is bright orange and rather ugly, but it reminds her that ability often grows through many small attempts.

listening.title: An Interview with a Sign Painter
listening.text:
Interviewer: Could you draw well as a child, Mr Saidov?
Painter: I could copy simple pictures, but I couldn't draw faces. Every person looked slightly surprised.
Interviewer: Could you paint large letters then?
Painter: Not at first. My father painted shop signs, and I watched him after school. By thirteen, I could paint neat capital letters with a wide brush.
Interviewer: What was difficult?
Painter: I couldn't keep the spacing even. Some words looked as if the letters were arguing and moving apart.
Interviewer: Could your father explain the spacing?
Painter: Yes, he could. He used pencil marks and showed me how to measure each gap.
Interviewer: Do you still use that method?
Painter: Often. Computers help with design now, but measuring carefully is still useful when the real wall isn't perfectly straight.

O‘tgan majburiyat, kelgusi zarurat va maslahatni uch mos shaklda yozadi.
80–110 so‘z yozadi; gaplarni bosh harf va tinish belgisi bilan ajratadi.

teacherNote: Oldindan: compulsory — majburiy; optional — ixtiyoriy; deposit — garov puli. Hafta oxirida shakl nomini aytmasdan vaziyat bering, o‘quvchi mos modalni tanlasin. Natijani ichki mashq bo‘yicha izohlang, standart imtihon balli sifatida bermang. O‘qish: avval mazmun, keyin uch javob dalilini belgilang. Tinglash: matnni yopib ikki marta o‘qing; avval vaziyat, keyin tafsilot. Sekin o‘quvchiga kalit so‘zlar va qo‘shimcha 30 soniya bering. Kuchli o‘quvchi yangi savol tuzib, matndan dalil ko‘rsatsin.

objective: May/might/could yordamida dalil va ehtimolni ajrataman.

reading.title: The Silent Noticeboard
reading.text: The noticeboard outside our community centre has been empty since Monday. Usually, it advertises language clubs, repairs and lost cats with surprisingly professional photographs. Several residents think the centre is closing, but the manager has not announced any closure. There are other possible explanations. The printer may be broken, or the volunteer may be away. The online calendar still shows three events for next week, although that information could be old. A cleaner saw a box of new drawing pins in the office yesterday. That detail suggests somebody plans to use the board again, but it does not prove when. I asked two neighbours before writing a message to the manager. One wanted to warn everyone immediately; the other preferred to wait. I chose a question rather than a warning. An empty board might mean a communication problem. It may not mean an empty building.

questions.prompt: What still shows three events? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “The online calendar still shows three events” — kalendar.

questions.prompt: What did the cleaner see? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
answers: a box of new drawing pins
questions.explanation: “A box of new drawing pins” — yangi knopkalar.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is supported: A definite closure or B uncertain cause? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “May not mean an empty building” va bir nechta taxmin sabab noaniqligini ko‘rsatadi.

listening.title: The Late Delivery
listening.text:
Mira: Our microphone hasn't arrived. The tracking page says it reached town yesterday, but the parcel could still be at the local office.
Owen: It might be at reception. Our receptionist sometimes accepts packages during lunch, and the message may not have reached us.
Mira: I checked reception. There is a box for the sports club, not ours. The driver may have used the side entrance.
Owen: That entrance is locked today. He might not know the new opening times. Let's contact the delivery office before we blame anyone.
Mira: Agreed. Our event starts tomorrow afternoon, so we still have time. I could ask the music club about a spare microphone.
Owen: Please do. Their equipment may be available, although they have a rehearsal tonight.
Mira: Then we have two tasks: locate the parcel and check a backup. Guessing alone won't make a microphone appear, however confidently we guess.

questions.prompt: When does the event start? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)

success: Ikki may/might/could taxmini bor.
Dalil va tasdiqlanmagan xulosa ajratiladi.
Bitta may not/might not va amaliy tekshiruv bor.

writing.prompt: 100–120 so‘zda markaz rahbariga yuborish uchun vaziyat tahlili paragrafini yozing: ikki sabab, dalil va keyingi qadam.
writing.model: The empty noticeboard may have a simple explanation. The printer could be broken, or the volunteer might be away this week. The online calendar still lists three events, so I do not think we should announce a closure. However, the calendar may not be current. The new drawing pins in the office suggest that someone intends to use the board again. I recommend asking the manager when the next notices will appear. We could also offer to write a temporary notice by hand. This would give residents useful information while we check the facts. A clear question is more helpful than a dramatic rumour.
success: 100–120 so‘z yozilgan.
Ikki ehtimol dalil bilan bog‘langan.

Sekin o‘quvchiga fact/may jadvali; ilg‘orga eng kuchli taxminni asoslatish. Scaffold: rather than — o‘rniga tayyor bog‘lanish; asosiy baho ehtimol modallariga.

objective: Must/can't bilan kuchli taxminni dalilga bog‘layman, Could …? bilan imkonni so‘rayman.

reading.title: The Extra Lunches
reading.text: At noon, the school kitchen had twelve extra lunches. The order sheet listed forty children, and the cook had prepared exactly forty meals. Only twenty-eight children were sitting in the dining room. The assistant first thought the missing group must be on a trip. However, the calendar showed no trip for that day. Then a teacher arrived carrying twelve empty trays. Her class was eating in the garden as part of a lesson about food waste. The lunches could not be unwanted: the class had specifically ordered them that morning. The assistant laughed at his own quick conclusion. Could the location of a meal matter as much as the number of meals? In this case, it did. He added a location column to the daily sheet. Counting carefully had not been enough; the team also needed to know where the children were. A full kitchen can still have an information gap.

questions.prompt: How many children were in the dining room? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Only twenty-eight children” — yigirma sakkiz.

questions.prompt: Where was the other class eating? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Her class was eating in the garden” — bog‘da.

questions.prompt: What column did the assistant add? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Added a location column” — joy ustuni.

listening.title: The Wrong Building
listening.text:
Nadia: Could this be the training centre? The number is right, but the sign says Dental Laboratory.
Peter: It can't be our centre. The invitation describes a building with a glass entrance, and this door is wooden.
Nadia: We must be on the wrong street. There are two streets with almost the same name: College Road and College Lane.
Peter: You're right. Our message says Lane. The map search selected Road automatically.
Nadia: The organiser must receive a lot of confused calls. There is a special note about the two addresses at the bottom of the invitation.
Peter: Perhaps, but the note only proves that confusion is possible. It doesn't tell us how many people call.
Nadia: Fair correction. Let's check the walking route. We have twenty minutes, and the real centre is only six minutes away. My confidence arrived before my reading skills today.

questions.prompt: What material is the actual door here? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “This door is wooden” — bu eshik yog‘och.

questions.prompt: Which street is the centre on? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Our message says Lane” — College Lane.

questions.explanation: Peter “It doesn't tell us how many people call” deb ikkinchi taxminni cheklaydi.

speaking.prompt: 90 soniyada manzil bo‘yicha ikki kuchli taxmin ayting; sherik dalilning kuchini tekshirsin.
success: Must va can't dalilga mos.
Could bilan bitta savol bor.
Bitta ortiqcha qat’iy xulosa yumshatiladi.

writing.prompt: 100–120 so‘zda tushlikdagi chalkashlikni hamkasblarga tushuntiruvchi tahliliy paragraf yozing.
writing.model: The twelve extra lunches must belong to the class in the garden. Their teacher brought twelve trays, and the class ordered food this morning. The meals can't simply be unwanted. Our first explanation about a school trip was not supported by the calendar. Could our daily sheet prevent this problem next time? I think it could, with a column for each group's eating location. Numbers alone do not explain where people are. The cook prepared the correct quantity, so we should not describe this as a cooking mistake. The problem was communication between the classroom and the kitchen, and a small change could make that communication clearer.
success: 100–120 so‘z bor.

Sekin o‘quvchiga evidence→deduction qolipi; ilg‘orga kuchli va kuchsiz must misolini baholatish. Scaffold: could not be bu hikoyada o‘tmishdagi imkonsizlik; faol topshiriqda hozirgi can't ishlatiladi.

objective: Hozir davom etayotgan taxmin va o‘tgan voqea taxminini modal shakllar bilan farqlayman.

reading.title: The Warm Printer
reading.text: When I entered the library office at seven, the printer was warm and a stack of certificates lay beside it. Nobody was there. The librarian must have printed them recently, I thought. Yet her coat was missing, and she usually arrives after eight. A volunteer might have come early instead. The computer screen showed a document called Garden Awards, but a filename could have remained open from the previous evening. I noticed a handwritten message: 'Please leave these for the breakfast group.' That explained the purpose, although not the person responsible. Someone might be preparing the ceremony downstairs now. I took the certificates to the kitchen and found the caretaker arranging flowers. He had printed them during his early shift. The machine's warmth had been useful evidence of recent activity, but it had not identified the user. A printer can reveal timing without revealing a name.

questions.prompt: What was beside the printer? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “A stack of certificates” — sertifikatlar.

questions.prompt: Who actually printed them? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “He had printed them” oldingi caretakerga ishora.

questions.explanation: “Useful evidence of recent activity” — yaqinda ishlatilganini, kimligini emas.

listening.title: A Closed Workshop
listening.text:
Rafi: The workshop door is locked, but I can hear a machine. They might be cutting wood in the back room.
Ella: They must have changed the entrance arrangements. A new sign points to the side gate.
Rafi: Or they could have locked this door just for the delivery. There is a truck outside.
Ella: True. The message on my phone says the session starts at two. I might have missed an update, though.
Rafi: Let's ring the bell at the side gate. We shouldn't stand here inventing a mystery about a perfectly ordinary door.
Ella: Someone is coming. She may be carrying the materials for our class.
Rafi: Yes, she has a box of safety glasses. The sound must have been a demonstration, not a full lesson. Still, we should ask rather than treat that as certain.
Ella: Agreed. Hearing a machine tells us something is happening, not exactly what.

questions.prompt: Where does the new sign point? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “Points to the side gate” — yon darvozaga.

Shaxs va vaqtga oid dalillar aralashtirilmagan.

writing.model: The workshop team might be preparing our materials in the back room. We can hear a machine, and a woman is carrying safety glasses. They may have moved the entrance because a delivery truck is outside the main door. The new sign must have been put there for a reason, but we do not yet know whether the change is permanent. Ella might have missed a message about it. We should ring the side bell and ask where to wait. The sound suggests activity, but it does not prove that our lesson has already started. reading.title: The Missing Booking
reading.text: Our debate team arrived at the hall and found a yoga class inside. We had booked the space by phone, but nobody had sent written confirmation. The manager checked the system: our request was still marked 'awaiting details'. We couldn't have completed the booking, because the final form was blank. I had assumed the phone conversation was enough. I should have asked for confirmation, and the office should have explained the final step clearly. We shouldn't have invited an audience before checking the room. Fortunately, the library offered us a smaller space. Some teammates wanted to blame one person, but that would have hidden the shared process problem. After the debate, we created a simple checklist with a named person for each stage. The yoga class kept its calm atmosphere; our team gained a practical lesson about paperwork without needing to practise any difficult poses.

questions.prompt: What was happening in the hall? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)

questions.explanation: “The library offered us a smaller space” — kutubxona.

listening.title: The Deleted Recording
listening.text:
Host: Our interview file is missing. I can't have deleted it this morning; I haven't opened the folder today.
Editor: I moved some files last night. I should have checked the names before moving them.
Host: We shouldn't have used titles like Final, Final New and Really Final. Those names are almost an invitation to confusion.
Editor: I agree. But moving is not deleting. The file could still be in the archive folder.
Host: Here it is, under Tuesday Interview. We should have included the guest's name and the date.
Editor: Let's rename it and make a backup before we edit. I am relieved, but this was avoidable.
Host: So am I. The guest gave us an hour of her time. Losing that would be more serious than losing our tidy desktop.
Editor: I'll write a short naming guide. No file should need to shout 'really final' at its neighbours.

questions.explanation: “I moved some files last night” — muharrir.

questions.explanation: “The guest's name and the date” — mehmon ismi va sana.

speaking.prompt: 90 soniyada bron xatosini ayblovsiz tahlil qiling: imkonsiz taxmin, qilinishi kerak bo‘lgan ish va qilinmasligi kerak bo‘lgan ish.

Tuzatish shaxsni ayblashdan ko‘ra jarayonga qaratilgan.

writing.model: We should have named the interview file with the guest's name and the recording date. Titles such as Really Final did not tell us enough. The host can't have deleted the file this morning because she did not open the folder. The editor moved it last night, and it was still safe in the archive. We shouldn't have assumed that a missing file was a deleted file. Before our next interview, we should agree on a naming system and a backup location. One person should check both copies after recording. This will protect the guest's contribution and save the team from another unnecessary search.

reading.title: A Festival without Enough Chairs
reading.text: Our film night attracted more visitors than expected. We could have borrowed chairs from the sports hall, but we decided the thirty seats in our room would be enough. Several people watched from the floor, and one cheerful visitor called it an unusually realistic camping film. The joke helped, but comfort still mattered. Next month, attendance is likely to rise because the local college is sharing our programme. Bad weather is unlikely to reduce numbers much; the event is indoors and close to a bus stop. We will probably need fifty chairs, although we should count registrations before arranging transport. The organiser definitely wants to keep entry free. That makes borrowing more suitable than buying. Our mistake was not a lack of options. We had an option and chose not to use it. A better estimate and an early phone call could prevent a repeat.

the local college is sharing their programme
local college is sharing their programme

questions.explanation: “Keep entry free” — kirish bepul.

listening.title: The Train We Didn't Take
listening.text:
Lena: We could have taken the direct train, but we chose the cheaper bus. Now we are arriving an hour later.
Sam: The delay is frustrating, but the price difference paid for lunch. I don't think the decision was completely unreasonable.
Lena: Fair point. Next time, the early train is likely to be busy because the exhibition opens at nine.
Sam: We should probably book seats a week ahead. Tickets are unlikely to become cheaper on the day.
Lena: I definitely don't want another journey with three changes.
Sam: Then let's compare the whole journey, not only the fare. A cheap ticket can cost time and energy.
Lena: Agreed. We still have four hours at the exhibition today, so the trip isn't ruined.
Sam: Exactly. We can learn from the choice without turning one late bus into a national transport disaster.

I definitely support keeping entry free. We should therefore ask the sports hall about borrowing chairs before considering a purchase. One volunteer can count bookings while another arranges collection. This approach uses evidence, protects our small budget and gives visitors a more comfortable evening.

reading.title: The Unclaimed Exhibition
reading.text: Three framed photographs arrived at our youth centre without a sender's note. They showed the old railway bridge, so they might belong to the local history group. However, the group's organiser denied sending them. A delivery label carried yesterday's date, which meant the parcel couldn't have been waiting in our office for weeks. We should have recorded the driver's details, but reception had been busy. The frames were new, and someone must have spent money preparing the pictures. That made throwing them into storage a poor response. We posted a neutral description online without publishing the photographs. By evening, a former member contacted us. She had intended them for next month's exhibition but had forgotten the note. We could have guessed correctly, yet a careful enquiry worked better. Clear labels are likely to become a firm rule for future donations, alongside a rather less official request for readable handwriting.

questions.explanation: “Showed the old railway bridge” — eski temiryo‘l ko‘prigi.

questions.prompt: Who sent them? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “A former member contacted us … She had intended them” — sobiq a’zo.

questions.prompt: What ruled out weeks in storage? (Qisqa javobni inglizcha yozing.)
questions.explanation: “A delivery label carried yesterday's date” — kechagi sana.

listening.title: The Quiet Ticket App
listening.text:
Manager: Online bookings have dropped, but the theatre may not be losing interest. The ticket app might be failing.
Analyst: The phone bookings are normal. That supports your idea. We should have tested the update before releasing it.
Manager: Could customers be giving up at the payment screen?
Analyst: Possibly. I tried twice, and both payments failed. The app can't be working reliably.
Manager: We could have kept the old version available, but we removed it too soon.
Analyst: The technician is checking it now. She is likely to find the problem today, though I can't promise a time.
Manager: Then we will probably direct customers to phone booking temporarily.
Analyst: Yes, and explain why. Silence may look like indifference. Customers should not need detective skills just to buy a seat for a comedy.
Manager: I'll prepare a brief notice with the phone number and an apology.
